title: Synthetic Seed Generation and Resampling Protocol for Eval Stability
author: Amelia Chen
body:
Overview

This document specifies Redwood's canonical protocol for generating synthetic seeds used by eval harnesses and for performing repeatable resampling during stress, stability, and regression tests. The goal is to reduce nondeterministic noise in eval results while preserving representative diversity across workloads and model variants. This protocol is intended for all eval-related automation (CI evals, nightly stress runs, private/dedicated shadowing, and benchmark suites).

Why we need a standardized seed/resampling protocol

- Eval instability is a major root cause of false positives in regression alerts and wasted developer time.
- Synthetic seeds and resampling policies control two orthogonal factors: reproducibility (exact-repeat debugging) and statistical representativeness (variance in distributional tests).
- Without standardization, teams use ad-hoc RNGs and sample sizes that lead to inconsistent F-score drift, noisy A/B comparisons, and fragile quantization verification.

Scope and applicability

- Applies to: eval-harness pipelines, prompt-set generators, synthetic workload producers, and model-onboarding testbeds.
- Out of scope: production request routing, customer data sampling (handled by data-management policies).

Key definitions

- seed: A 64-bit integer used as the root for deterministic PRNG chains.
- deterministic run: An eval execution that, given the same seed and config, must produce byte-for-byte identical synthetic inputs and stable metric computations (modulo model stochasticity when sampling is enabled).
- resample window: The policy time interval after which new synthetic seeds are introduced into continuous evals (e.g., daily, weekly).

Ownership and responsibilities

- Eval Platform (team): maintain the seed service, canonical RNG libraries, and automation for resampling. Owner: @eval-platform.
- Applied ML / Evals (team): define per-workload seed distributions, target sample sizes, and required statistical tests. Owner: @applied-ml.
- Model Onboarding Engineers: request additional deterministic seeds for debugging and certify new seed sets during model promotions.

Protocol: Seed generation and cataloging

1) Canonical RNG and format
   - Use the platform canonical PRNG: xoshiro256++ initialized from a 64-bit master seed. Implementations exist in Redwood's eval-sdks (python and go) at git:redwood/eval-sdks (module: redwood.eval.rng).
   - Seed metadata record (stringified JSON) must include: seed_id, seed_value (decimal), created_by, created_at (ISO-8601), tags (list), and checksum. Example: {\"seed_id\":\"sd-20260214-17\",\"seed_value\":\"9571623412341234\",\"created_by\":\"eval-platform\",\"created_at\":\"2026-02-14T17:23:00Z\",\"tags\":[\"nl-fewshot\",\"stress\"],\"checksum\":\"sha256:...\"}.

2) Seed catalog service
   - All seeds must be registered in the seed-catalog (internal HTTP API: seed-catalog.redwood.svc.cluster.local).
   - Seed records are immutable; if a seed is revoked, mark status=deprecated with a deprecation_reason.

3) Namespacing and tag schema
   - Use a three-part tag schema: workload-type (e.g., \"nl-classification\"), purpose (e.g., \"canary\", \"stress\"), and geography/locale (optional, e.g., \"en-US\").

4) Entropy and diversity constraints
   - For each synthetic workload generator, maintain a mapping of entropy budgets (percentiles of prompt template parameterization). The eval team must define minimum coverage constraints (e.g., template coverage >= 95% over canonical prompt set).

Resampling policy and cadence

- Static evals (on PR): use fixed seed sets pinned in the PR config file. Re-run behavior must re-use the same seeds until the PR author updates the config.
- CI nightly/every-24h stress: rotate N seeds per workload where N depends on workload variance (see table below).
- Weekly/Canary pool: refresh 20% of the pool every week; full pool refresh every 12 weeks or when prompt-set changes exceed a threshold.

Resampling cadence table

| Eval type | Pool size (min) | Refresh policy | Rationale |
|-----------|-----------------|----------------|-----------|
| PR/unit (deterministic) | 8 | pinned per PR | Fast short runs; reproducibility prioritized |
| CI/nightly stress | 128 | rotate 8 seeds/day | Capture diversity; limit noise per run |
| Production shadow | 512 | rotate 64 seeds/day | Extensive coverage for real traffic emulation |
| Long-tail detection suite | 2048 | stratified monthly resample | Find edge-case regressions |

Statistical guidance and thresholds

- Minimum effective sample size (ESS): each eval-run must compute ESS for weighted metrics; ESS < 30 flags low-confidence.
- Metric variance threshold: 95th percentile rolling variance (7-day window) per-metric must remain below workload-specific thresholds. If variance > threshold, trigger triage flow.
- Regression alerting: require both (a) metric delta >= critical_delta and (b) p-value <= 0.01 using the recommended bootstrap test. Avoid single-run-based alerts.

Configuration examples

- YAML example for an eval job that consumes seed-catalog:

job_name: stress-qa-nl
workload: nl-generation
seed_pool: seed-catalog:tag=\"nl-generation,stress,en-US\"
pool_size: 128
rotate_per_run: 8
metrics: [bleu,rouge2,semantic-similarity]
critical_delta: 0.06
variance_thresholds:
  bleu: 0.02
  semantic-similarity: 0.015

CLI examples

- Create a new seed and register: 
  redwood-seed create --tags nl-generation,stress --created-by automated-resampler --output-json | curl -X POST \
    -H 'Content-Type: application/json' --data @- https://seed-catalog.internal/api/v1/seeds

- Pull seed pool for job: 
  redwood-seed list --tags \"nl-generation,stress,en-US\" --limit 128 --format csv

Deterministic debug mode

- For failures that require exact replay, request the seed_id and run with --deterministic --seed-id <seed_id> flags. Deterministic runs use the same RNG chain and template parameterization, ensuring byte-for-byte identical synthetic inputs.

Integration with other eval concerns

- Quantization tests: tag seeds used for quant-eval as \"quant-sanity\"; keep a small dedicated pool (min 64) that is never rotated during a quant certification run to isolate numeric instability from sampling noise.
- Regression triage: link seed_id in regression tickets. The triage playbook should include steps to re-run failing workloads with the exact seed and with a nearby neighborhood of +/- 10 seeds to determine whether the failure is seed-specific or systematic.
- Prompt coverage: every resample must compute prompt-template coverage delta and fail if coverage falls below 90% of the canonical set.

Failure modes and runbook pointers

- Symptom: high day-to-day metric variance without code or model changes.
  - Quick checks: verify seed-catalog returned the expected pool; check for unintended stochastic sampling flags; confirm PRNG library version.
  - If seed drift suspected: pin to earlier seed_id and re-run. See runbook: /confluence/applied-ml-and-evals/eval-harness/promotion-readiness-synthetic-quant-safety-playbook-2026

- Symptom: single-seed outliers causing regression alerts.
  - Triage: re-run with deterministic seed; run neighborhood of seeds (+/- 10); if only one seed fails, mark seed as flakey and deprecate in seed-catalog, then expand pool to maintain coverage.

Monitoring, dashboards, and SLOs

- Dashboards to create:
  - Eval Stability Overview: per-workload rolling variance, ESS, seed-pool utilization.
  - Seed Health: seed success rate, flakiness per-seed_id (failures/total runs), average runtime impact.

- SLOs:
  - Per-run ESS >= 50 for nightly stress (target) and ESS >= 30 (minimum).
  - Per-workload 7-day variance under threshold defined in workload config (default 0.03).
  - Seed catalog API 99.9% availability with 200ms median latency.

Rollout and updates

1) New seed sets must go through a staged rollout: 
   - Stage A (canary): 5% of nightly runs for 7 days, monitor variance and coverage.
   - Stage B (gradual): 25% for 14 days.
   - Stage C (full): 100% after no significant anomalies.
2) If any monitoring alert fires during canary, rollback to previous seed pool and open an incident with applied-ml and eval-platform.

Appendix: quick checklist for model-onboarding engineers

- [ ] Request private deterministic seeds for debugging (include seed_id in PR).
- [ ] Verify that quant-eval tag pool is used for numeric regressions.
- [ ] Run neighborhood resamples when investigating flaky failures.
- [ ] Record seed_id in the promotion ticket and note any deprecations.

References and related docs

- seed-catalog API: https://seed-catalog.internal/docs
- eval-sdks (rng implementation): git:redwood/eval-sdks#rng
- Promotion readiness playbook: /confluence/applied-ml-and-evals/model-onboarding/inference-readiness-eval-matrix-and-promotion-playbook-2026
